chunks: And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:
"The most beloved companions to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are four; and no group exceeds seven except that their commotion becomes much."

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةٌ: four, described here as the most beloved number of companions
key_terms.الصَّحَابَةِ: companions or fellow associates in company
key_terms.سَبْعَةٍ: seven, the upper limit mentioned before commotion increases
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic, a reverential description of Allah
key_terms.لَغَطُهُمْ: their noise, commotion, or confused uproar

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the ideal number of companions in a group?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches moderation in the size of a traveling or companion group, indicating that a smaller number is more conducive to harmony and order. It highlights a social ethic in which limited group size helps reduce noise, confusion, and disorder among companions.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2444 - The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family) said:
"The most beloved companions to Allah, the Almighty, are four. And any group that exceeds seven will have excessive commotion."
